questions.question: Using the standard two-stack queue design (S1 for enqueue, S2 for dequeue), trace: enqueue(1), enqueue(2), dequeue(), enqueue(3), dequeue(), dequeue(). What values are dequeued, in order?
questions.solutionApproach: enqueue 1,2: S1=[1,2]. dequeue: S2 empty, pour S1 into S2 (order reverses) so 1 is on top; pop 1. enqueue 3: S1=[3]. dequeue: S2 still has 2, pop 2. dequeue: S2 empty, pour S1 into S2, pop 3. Output 1,2,3.

questions.question: A circular queue has capacity 5 (indices 0-4). front=2, rear=4. After one more enqueue, what is the new rear index?
A queue is implemented as a CIRCULAR singly linked list with only ONE external pointer, to the REAR node. Can both enqueue and dequeue be done in O(1)?
questions.solutionApproach: Yes — rear->next gives the front node directly (circular structure). Enqueue: insert after rear, update rear. Dequeue: remove rear->next (the front), update rear->next to skip it. Both O(1) despite only one external pointer.
questions.answer: Yes, both O(1) — the classic 'single rear pointer, circular list' trick.
